Summarize a composition-as-predictor model

Source: R/summary_comp_iv.R
summary.comp_iv.Rd

Tabulates the omnibus test of the whole composition of a comp_iv() fit and one "part vs remaining" effect per part. Each effect is the rotated model's ilr1 coefficient, or its slope at the reference composition (see Details), back-transformed to the model's effect scale. Printing the result shows a text report, as with summary.lm(), and pub_ready() builds a publication gt table from it.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'comp_iv'
summary(object, conf_level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

object

A comp_iv object from comp_iv().

conf_level

Confidence level for the per-part Wald intervals.

...

Unused; present for S3 consistency.

Value

An object of class summary_comp_iv, printed as a text report by print.summary_comp_iv() and passed to pub_ready() for a gt table. A list with elements:

global

The one-row omnibus composition test.

per_part

The per-part effect table: one row per part, or per part and non-reference outcome category for a multinomial fit. It shares the columns parameter, label, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value with global, whose estimate/conf.low/conf.high are NA. label carries the part's display label (or its raw name). A per-category model (multinomial) adds response_level.

moderation

The joint moderation Wald test when the fit was built with a moderator, else NULL. A moderated fit also gives per_part three further columns (mod_statistic, mod_df, mod_p.value). They hold the joint Wald test of that part's own ilr1 : moderator coefficient(s), which asks whether the part's effect varies by moderator level; the moderation test pools every part. Like the per-part effect rows, they are descriptive and carry no multiplicity adjustment. An unmoderated fit omits them.

curvature_test

The joint Wald test of the squares and products of the coordinates when the fit holds the full quadratic (see the curvature_test element of comp_iv()), else NULL.

convergence

A list of the fit's status one-row tibble (converged, singular, n_warnings) and its warnings tibble of captured backend conditions.

icc

For a clustered fit, a tibble with one row per grouping term (group, variance, measure, value), read from the fit's own variance components. For "lmer" and "rlmer", value is each term's share of the total variance, the intraclass correlation \(v_g / (\sum_h v_h + \sigma^2)\), where the sum runs over all grouping terms \(h\). A logit- or probit-link binomial "glmer" and an ordinal "clmm" give its latent-scale form, with \(\pi^2/3\) (logit) or 1 (probit) in place of \(\sigma^2\). A "coxme" fit gives the median hazard ratio \(\exp(\sqrt{2 v_g}\, \Phi^{-1}(0.75))\): the median, over pairs of clusters, of the hazard ratio between two individuals with identical covariates, one from each cluster, taken from the higher-risk cluster to the lower-risk one (Austin et al. 2017). measure is "not available" and value NA for the other clustered engines, for a log-link binomial "glmer", which has no latent-scale form, and for a "glmer" of any other family. NULL for a fit without a random term.

total_test, total_beta

With include_total = TRUE, the one-row Wald test of the t_total coefficient and its fitted value on the link scale (the first category's for a multinomial fit, whose test is joint); NULL otherwise.

per_part_slopes

Present, and TRUE, only when at least one per-part row is a slope at the reference composition rather than a coefficient.

per_part_no_slope

The reason, as text, why emmeans::emtrends() gave no slope and those rows are NA. Present only in that case.

labels, effect_measure, conf_level, moderator, fit_label, total, model_type, omnibus

Carried through for print.summary_comp_iv() and pub_ready().

units

The composition's unit label, printed after total; NULL when none was declared.

Details

The effect scale is a hazard ratio for a Cox model, a cumulative odds ratio for an ordinal model and a relative-risk ratio for a multinomial model. A GLM's scale follows its link: an odds ratio (logit), a rate, risk or mean ratio (log) or a mean difference (identity). Every linear engine reports a mean difference.

For mixed models the per-part effects come from one refit per part (stored at fit time in object$models), so building this summary does no extra fitting. For an "lmer" fit, each per-part standard error, interval and p-value uses the degrees-of-freedom method that emmeans uses for predict_realloc() on the same fit. The default is the Kenward-Roger approximation through pbkrtest. The Satterthwaite approximation through lmerTest is used when emmeans::emm_options(lmer.df =) selects it, or when pbkrtest is absent, disabled or the fit has more observations than emmeans::emm_options(pbkrtest.limit =). Both pbkrtest and lmerTest are optional, and when neither applies, or emmeans::emm_options(lmer.df = "asymptotic") is set, the degrees of freedom are asymptotic (normal). "glmer", "coxme" and "rlmer" rows are asymptotic, as their emmeans predictions are (robustlmm reports no degrees of freedom).

When the formula gives the composition non-linear terms (see ilr()), a product of coordinates or no main effect, a rotated fit has no single ilr1 coefficient to read. Each per-part effect is then the slope of its linear predictor in ilr1 at the reference composition, from emmeans::emtrends(), back-transformed in the same way, and the printed report says so. With a composition-by-covariate interaction as well, that slope is the equal-weight average over the covariate's levels. An engine for which emtrends() gives no such slope ("mblogit", "lmrob") reports NA rows.

References

Austin, P. C., Wagner, P., & Merlo, J. (2017). The median hazard ratio: A useful measure of variance and general contextual effects in multilevel survival analysis. Statistics in Medicine, 36(6), 928-938. doi:10.1002/sim.7188

Goldstein, H., Browne, W., & Rasbash, J. (2002). Partitioning variation in multilevel models. Understanding Statistics, 1(4), 223-231. doi:10.1207/S15328031US0104_02

Kenward, M. G., & Roger, J. H. (1997). Small sample inference for fixed effects from restricted maximum likelihood. Biometrics, 53(3), 983-997. doi:10.2307/2533558

See also

comp_iv() to fit the model; plot.comp_iv() for the predicted-outcome surface; predict_realloc() for reallocation predictions; pub_ready() for a formatted gt table built from this summary.

Other composition as predictor: comp_iv(), plot.comp_iv()

Examples

cd <- declare_composition(timeuse, c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"),
                          closure = 1440)
m <- comp_iv(cd, outcome = "obesity", model = "glm", family = "binomial")
s <- summary(m)
s$per_part
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>   parameter         label estimate conf.low conf.high     p.value
#>   <chr>             <chr>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 MVPA vs remaining MVPA     0.501    0.382     0.656 0.000000489
#> 2 LPA vs remaining  LPA      0.982    0.506     1.91  0.958      
#> 3 SB vs remaining   SB       2.98     1.16      7.65  0.0234     
#> 4 SPT vs remaining  SPT      0.683    0.273     1.71  0.415
